input.question: Why does it take hours to install big programs and games but seconds to uninstall it?
input.ground_truth: When you are installing a game, you are writing the files to your hard drive. It has to remember where to access those files. The uninstallation is just forgetting those locations on your drive, not actually erasing them.

Question: Why does it take hours to install big programs and games but seconds to uninstall it?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a big box of LEGO bricks. When you want to build something big with the LEGO bricks, like a huge castle, it takes a long time because you have to find every single brick, put them in the right place, and make sure everything fits just right.

But when you want to put the LEGO castle away, you just pick up the whole castle and put it in the box. That’s much faster!

Installing a big program or game is like building the LEGO castle—it has to put lots of little pieces in the right spots on your computer, which takes time.

Uninstalling it is like putting the castle back in the box. The computer just knows where all the pieces go, so it can take them away much faster.
